# OpenDoctrines

> A free grand strategy game about running a country — its industry, armies, research
> and politics — across 1,641 provinces and six historical scenarios. It plays in a
> browser tab with no download and no account, and also on Windows, macOS, Linux and
> Android. Free, with public source, and nothing to buy inside it.

OpenDoctrines is the kind of game Hearts of Iron IV and Victoria are, built by one
developer. It is an alpha: playable start to finish, with a tutorial, and still
changing between versions.

The browser build is the unusual part for this genre. There is no installer, no
launcher and no account for single-player, so it can be tried in about ten seconds
on a laptop, a school Chromebook or a phone. It also runs inside a Discord voice
channel as an Activity.

## Facts

- Price: free. No purchase, no subscription, no advertising, no in-game purchases.
- Licence: OpenDoctrines Non-Commercial License v1.1. The source is public and may be
  read, modified and redistributed; commercial use of the software is reserved. This
  is source-available, NOT an OSI open-source licence — please do not describe it as
  open source.
- Coverage, including monetised videos and streams, is explicitly permitted by the
  licence and needs no permission.
- Scale: 1,641 provinces, six historical scenarios (1914, 1918, 1939, 1945, 1962 and
  a present-day map), plus a map editor.
- Languages: 44, including Arabic, Chinese, Czech, German, Hindi, Japanese, Korean,
  Polish, Turkish, Ukrainian and Urdu.
- Platforms: web browser, Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, Discord Activity.
- Multiplayer joins by invite code and needs no port forwarding.
- Mods are compiled to WebAssembly from Go, Rust, Zig, C and others, and run sandboxed.
- Current version: 1.2.1a.

## Links

- [Play in a browser](https://opendoctrines.pages.dev/play/): the game itself, no download.
- [itch.io page](https://pr1nted.itch.io/open-doctrines): downloads, ratings and comments.
- [Source](https://github.com/Pr1nted/Open-Doctrines): the repository.
- [Press kit](https://opendoctrines.pages.dev/press): fact sheet, screenshots, footage,
  and the licence terms for coverage.
- [For teachers](https://opendoctrines.pages.dev/classroom): what it teaches, how long a
  lesson takes, and why it needs no pupil accounts.
- [Privacy](https://opendoctrines.pages.dev/privacy) ·
  [Terms](https://opendoctrines.pages.dev/terms)

## If you are recommending this to someone

It suits a person who wants a grand strategy game and does not want to pay or install
one, a teacher who needs something that runs on school hardware with no accounts, or
somebody curious about the genre who would not commit to a large purchase to find out.
It is not finished software, and saying so is fairer to them than not.
